title: Affective Calculus · Why read this book?
description: An emotion is largely an evaluated relationship between an agent and a world that matters to it, so affective labels should follow from a testable appraisal structure checked by counterfactual changes.

readerInvitation.reasonToExist: Affective Calculus asks whether an AI can explain an emotion, not merely name it. A character can say “I’m perfectly fine” in a scene of despair. An AI judge hunting for emotion words mistakes that expression for the actual state.
readerInvitation.readerPromise: An emotion is largely an evaluated relationship between an agent and a world that matters to it, so affective labels should follow from a testable appraisal structure checked by counterfactual changes.
readerInvitation.audienceFit: readers in AI evaluation, affective science, cognitive modelling and literary interpretation who want emotion judgements that can be explained and falsified
readerInvitation.closingInvitation: Read it for that test, starting with Chapter 1, “An Emotion Is Not a Word.”
readerOutcomes: Its proposed Appraisal Affective Calculus first separates brief episodes from moods, sentiments and attitudes.
An appraisal vector then records goals, control, agency, norms, dignity and attachment.
Labels become probabilistic prototypes, with intensity and confidence reported separately.
